svg.text: This models the aircraft dynamics with control from the softwalls algorithm. The aircraft and softwall are drawn as graphics, and the user acts as a pilot by using the left and right arrow keys.
This is the aircraft dynamics model.
This generates the aircraft and softwall images.
This displays the aircraft with the current orientation in the middle of the screen.
This creates the aircraft from simple components and scales it down to fit the screen.
The fuselage is a cylinder plus a cone
The vertical stabilizer is drawn from a rotated prism.
The wings are made from a single prism object.
The horizontal stabilizer is made from a prism.
This orients the aircraft to the correct heading and bank angle.
PI/2 is added so the aircraft of heading 0 faces East.
Here we draw the no-fly zone as a cylinder with its top at equal level to the middle of the aircraft.
This generates the pilot's desired change in heading. It's response is dampened by the integrator to feel more realistic.
This creates a signal which is 1 while the left arrow is pressed, -1 while the right arrow is pressed, and 0 while both or neither are pressed.
The director is synchronized to real time, so that a key press held for one second will respond as if it were held for one second.

svg.text: This computes the bias using the implicit surface representation of the reachable set.
This takes in the state and computes the implicit surface function. The value and gradient are returned.

entity.name: ImplicitSurface
entity.doc: A view screen with a mountain backdrop.

svg.text: Given the function value, this calculates the magnitude of the bias to apply. The function value represents the distance from the reachable set, and the bias distance is the distance at which to begin adding bias.

[-11.07; 0.0; 0.0] is approximately on the boundary of the reachable set. To make the bias region last for 0.5, when approaching the no-fly zone head-on, we chose the biasDistance from the value at [-11.57; 0.0; 0.0].
This takes the dot product (divided by dPhiDTheta) of the implicit surface gradient and the time-derivate of the current state, assuming 0 bias is applied.
Takes the cosine and sine of the heading angle.
Computes the optimal bias required to steer the aircraft away from the reachable set.
This assumes the calculation is possible, and the optimal control is bounded in magnitude by maxHeadingDot.
